opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building and improving the AXON ad platform — down 56% YoY, because last year's figure still carried costs of the apps business that has since been sold.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling the platform to advertisers and app publishers — down 30% YoY after the apps sale shrank the company.

follow100Note: The 'other expense' step nets $48M of income from the sold apps business against $74M of interest and other costs — see the note under the chart. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: AppLovin reports as a single segment. The apps business it sold in June 2025 is reported as discontinued operations: its $48M contribution is folded into the 'other' step of the flow so the bottom line matches the reported net income of $820M; the continuing platform earned $772M.
oneTimers: Income of $48M from the apps business AppLovin sold in June 2025, reported as discontinued operations — its last contribution, including the gain on the sale.
otherDetail: Interest expense of $51M on AppLovin's debt, plus $22M of other expense, net — partly offset by $48M of income from the apps business sold in June, which accounting rules report as discontinued operations.

segments.name: Advertising platform
segments.note: Ads placed through AppLovin's AXON platform — advertisers pay to reach users inside other companies' apps, and AXON's AI decides which ads to show. AppLovin sold its own apps business in June 2025, so this platform is now the whole company.

takeaways.text: Revenue grew 77% to $1.26B as advertisers kept shifting budgets to AXON, AppLovin's AI ad platform. The comparison is clean — the sold apps business counts as discontinued operations in both periods, so this is the platform's own growth.
takeaways.title: Growth stayed hot

takeaways.text: Net income of $820M is 65% of revenue, up 164% in a year. The platform itself earned $772M from continuing operations; the apps business added a final $48M in the quarter it was sold.
takeaways.title: Most of it became profit

takeaways.text: Free cash flow was $768M in a single quarter. AppLovin spent $1.27B buying back its own shares across the first half of 2025.
takeaways.title: Cash in, buybacks out

verdict: AppLovin grew revenue 77% to $1.26B as its AXON ad platform kept surging, and net income more than doubled to $820M — including a final $48M contribution from the apps business it sold in June.
